missionPremise: Reading (a) or reading (b) of _dispatches/2026-09-17_p306-williamson-coverage-keyspace_dispatch.md is what produced Williamson 48491's COUNTY_COVERAGE_COLLAPSE refusal at 2026-09-17T15:03:50Z (run 59808bfc, staging publish factory-bastrop-publish-99pbp, publish image f476f438, factory b65f61b plus P-276). The floor is P-236 `MIN_COVERAGE_RETENTION` 0.95 in hauska-factory src/lib/publish-coverage-floor.mjs; its header's premise — 'the two sides are the same predicate on the same column' — is the sentence under test (dispatch line 208).

theTwoReadings.a: The floor compares ONE id keyspace with TWO. The served tier-1 set holds a numeric id set and an R-prefixed id set; the source table txgio_parcel is R-keyed. The comparison therefore divides a one-namespace numerator by a two-namespace denominator.
theTwoReadings.b: The bake would strip zoning. It reads zoning keyed on R-prefixed accounts, finds nothing for the live numeric nodes, and would write them zoning-absent — the 147,145 numeric nodes zoned today would lose their district.
theTwoReadings.notExclusive: The dispatch says they are not exclusive. The design measured both independently rather than treating one as the other's explanation.

preRegisteredPredictions.quoted: If (a) holds, the served zoned count with retired rows excluded is within five percent of the source count or above it.
preRegisteredPredictions.whatWouldProveItWrong: A served-zoned-with-retired-excluded count that sits outside +/-5% of the source count and below it would leave reading (a) unsupported in the currency the dispatch chose.

preRegisteredPredictions.quoted: If (b) holds, at least one of the five named numeric parcels has no zoning row the bake can reach by its own key.
preRegisteredPredictions.whatWouldProveItWrong: All five reaching a zoning row by the bake's own key path falsifies (b) for those parcels.

preRegisteredPredictions.quoted: If you open a PR: the new test fails on today's numbers without the fix, and a control fixture with a genuine collapse on one keyspace still refuses COUNTY_COVERAGE_COLLAPSE.
preRegisteredPredictions.whatWouldProveItWrong: A test that passes with and without the fix (decorative), or a control that the scoping rescues (a weakened floor).

preRegisteredPredictions.statement: The source side must be MEASURABLY single-keyspace. If txgio_parcel for 48491 holds a material numeric set, keyspace scoping is not a valid fix and this lane opens NO PR.
If the refusal is a genuine collapse inside the source's own keyspace (served R-prefixed zoned materially above source R-prefixed zoned), then the floor is right and the fix is wrong — no PR.

The fix must not change the threshold, must not name 48491, must fall back to the whole-count comparison whenever the shape does not match, and must RECORD the rows and keyspaces it excludes rather than dropping them quietly (the instrument's exclusion set is part of its contract, DEV_PROCESS).

adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.q: A1 — is the source keyspace actually single, or am I about to assert a scope that does not exist?
adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.disposition: Decided BEFORE measuring: P4 above. If the source had held a material numeric set, no PR. Answer in CP2 (source: 304,162 R + 136 other + 0 numeric).

adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.q: A2 — could the refusal be a genuine collapse that a keyspace story would explain away?
adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.disposition: P5. The discriminator is the SAME ratio computed inside one keyspace: if the served R side exceeded the source R side by more than 5%, the floor would be right and the fix wrong.

adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.q: A3 — is the dispatch's falsifier 1 even expressed in the floor's currency?
adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.disposition: Flagged at design time as the design's sharpest risk: retention in this floor is sourceZoned/servedZoned (code line 551), so 'the served count is within five percent of the source count' is a COUNT equality test, while the floor's operative test is a RATIO crossing 0.95. A reading can hold while falsifier 1 is contradicted. The design therefore committed to reporting both, separately, rather than choosing whichever passed.

adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.q: A4 — does scoping weaken the floor?
adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.disposition: P6. Three enforceable commitments: no threshold change; no county named in code; scoping only engages when the source is measurably single-keyspace AND the served side carries a per-keyspace breakdown, else fall back to the existing whole-count comparison; the excluded rows and keyspaces are recorded in the verdict.

adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.q: A5 — is the 2026-09-10 retirement of the R-prefixed nodes the cause, or a second symptom of the same keyspace mismatch?
adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.disposition: Held open at design time rather than assumed. The dispatch's reading (a) attributes the inflated denominator to the retired R rows; if the R rows are in the SOURCE's own keyspace they cannot be 'a population the source side never sees'. Measured in CP2 — the attribution is the one thing this lane reversed.

adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.q: A6 — what would make this lane's PR unsafe to merge?
adversarialQuestionsAskedOfMyOwnDesign.disposition: The residual named in CP2: with scoping, the served population in the keyspace the source table cannot key (numeric, 147,145 zoned) is outside the floor's comparison. It is recorded, not dropped, but the guard for that population is the readiness gate's bakeVsRoll arm, not this floor. Stated for the integration seat to weigh.
